conviction_note: Q3 drivers (normal wind vs a below-norm Q3 2025, Revolution Wind and Greater Changhua 2b&4 ramping, ~DKK 3.5bn rate-driven impairment) were all flagged by Ørsted's own 8 Oct pre-close call, so the quarter is priced; the 'above DKK 28bn' guide is most likely reiterated, a raise is plausible but unsourced, and the stock rose ~7% on the US midterms the day before the print, so p_up sits at 52 on a 4.5% scale; findings sum +0.1 and the scaled +0.18 agree in sign and size.

already_public.what: FY2026 guidance: EBITDA excl. new partnerships and cancellation fees above DKK 28bn, gross investments DKK 50-55bn, reaffirmed with H1 (H1 EBITDA excl. DKK 15.0bn, +8%)

Q3 2026 pre-close call: guide still above DKK 28bn; offshore higher, onshore in line, Bioenergy & Other lower; Q3 offshore wind speeds around portfolio norms; Revolution Wind and Greater Changhua 2b & 4 ramping in Q3; US 10y up ~75bp in Q3 implying ~DKK 3.5bn additional non-cash impairments all else equal; 2027 EBITDA target above DKK 32bn
Dividend reinstated for FY2026, level only in Annual Report 2026
Release date and time confirmed: Q3 2026 on 5 Nov at ~08:00 CET; installed offshore capacity now 11 GW (10.2 GW in the August release)

new_in_release.expect: Q3 EBITDA excl. new partnerships up clearly year on year against a weak Q3 2025 (about DKK 3.1bn, derived from 9M 17.0 minus H1 13.9), helped by normal wind and new capacity. The direction against consensus is unknown because no Q3 consensus could be sourced.
'above DKK 28bn' most likely reiterated. There is some chance of a raise or a firmer point (strong H1, offshore guided higher, high Q3 power prices at peers). A cut looks unlikely.

Net profit hit by a non-cash US impairment of roughly DKK 3.5bn, which was pre-flagged. The US update (Revolution Wind permit remand, Sunrise Wind H2 2027) is read in light of the 4 Nov midterm result.
unknown; heavy capex (DKK 50-55bn guide) and Q2 operating cash flow down 64% y/y
No level expected; it is due with the Annual Report 2026.

bar: The company's FY2026 guide is EBITDA excl. new partnerships and cancellation fees above DKK 28bn (https://www.inderes.dk/releases/orsted-continues-its-strategic-progress-delivers-solid-operational-performance-and-is-on-track-to-deliver-on-its-2026-financial-guidance). Morningstar put Feb-2026 FY consensus at DKK 28.5bn (https://global.morningstar.com/en-nd/stocks/orsted-earnings-good-operational-performance-2026-guidance-confirmed-shares-fairly-valued). The Q3-specific consensus is unsourced, so the quarter-level findings are capped small. The only quarter number found is MarketBeat's ADR EPS of $0.1056 (https://www.dailypolitical.com/2026/11/04/orsted-a-s-dnngy-projected-to-post-earnings-on-thursday.html), a single unverified source.
session_check: bmo. Ørsted's own announcement of 2026-10-29 says the Q3 2026 results will be released at approximately 08:00 CET on Thursday 5 November 2026, with the call at 14:00 CET: https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=bd210f5974f7deab642cd95f7019da6c0&lang=en&src=listed
positioning_check: The baseline's 0.0 is a name-join miss. The DFSA (Finanstilsynet) aggregated net short table, read 2026-11-04, lists 'DK0060094928 Ørsted A/S 0,54', latest reported change 15-10-2026 (https://www.dfsa.dk/financial-themes/capital-market/company-announcements/aggregated-net-short-positions). On Denmark's 0.1% threshold that is a small, uncrowded short, unchanged for about three weeks, so it is neither building nor covering into the print. No squeeze fuel.

findings.finding: On its 8 Oct pre-close call Ørsted said Q3 2026 offshore wind speeds were around portfolio norms (Q3 2025 was below norm), with Revolution Wind and Greater Changhua 2b & 4 ramping in Q3. Installed offshore capacity went from 10.2 GW (Aug) to 11 GW (29 Oct release), so Q3 EBITDA should rise clearly year on year, but every driver was pre-released.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Quarterly EBITDA surprises have moved the stock both ways: Q2 2026 beat on Hornsea 3 construction earnings, Q1 2026 was strong. The baseline's estimated reaction history has a median of 3.07% and is a lower bound.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced. The company told the analysts on the pre-close call, so consensus already carries the normal wind and the ramp-ups. What would remain unpriced is the size of the ramp contribution, which only the release shows. Since there is no visible Q3 consensus, the gap cannot be measured.
findings.independence: Vattenfall's Q3 2026 report (29 Oct) shows offshore wind volumes slightly higher y/y on unchanged 4,454 MW offshore capacity ('Electricity generation increased by 4% due to slightly higher volumes from offshore wind power'). That fits a normal-wind Q3: https://group.vattenfall.com/siteassets/corporate/investors/interim_reports/2026/vattenfall-q3-report-2026.pdf

findings.finding: Ørsted pre-flagged that the ~75bp rise in the US 10-year yield in Q3 2026 implies about DKK 3.5bn of additional non-cash impairments on US projects, all else equal. Net profit will carry a large write-down the market was told to expect.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 carried a DKK 1.2bn net impairment for the same reason, and the release was read on EBITDA and the reaffirmed guide. The 2023-2025 US write-downs moved the stock heavily when they were unflagged; this one is flagged.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is the company's own sensitivity, given on the pre-close. Only a write-down materially above ~DKK 3.5bn (a project-specific charge on Sunrise or Revolution Wind on top of rates) would be news, and nothing sourced points to one.
findings.independence: The H1 report shows the same mechanism already at work: H1 impairments of DKK 2.5bn and Q2 of DKK 1.2bn. https://www.inderes.dk/releases/orsted-continues-its-strategic-progress-delivers-solid-operational-performance-and-is-on-track-to-deliver-on-its-2026-financial-guidance

findings.finding: Peer evidence of a high-price Q3: Vattenfall's Wind segment underlying EBITDA rose to SEK 4,370m from 2,657m in Q3 2026 (+64%) on roughly flat volumes, and group Q3 underlying operating profit rose 320% 'driven by higher electricity prices'. Together with Ørsted's own 'Offshore higher' segment outlook, this gives a modest case that the 'above DKK 28bn' guide is firmed or raised.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Ørsted's guidance changes have been the large movers (2023-2025 cuts and impairments). Reiterations, as in H1 2026 and Q1 2026, gave moderate moves of roughly 2-4% in the baseline's estimated history.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a peer-to-company transmission, so it is a hypothesis. Most of Ørsted's offshore output sits under CfDs, subsidies or hedges, so the merchant upside is partial. Had the market priced a raise, the sell-side would be quoting a FY number well above 28bn. The only sourced consensus (Feb, DKK 28.5bn) sits just above the floor of the guide.
findings.independence: Ørsted's pre-close (8 Oct) says the segment outlook is 'higher for Offshore', and the H1 report attributes offshore growth to 'higher wind speeds and higher prices': https://quartr.com/companies/rsted_3520

findings.finding: The disclosed short is small and unmoved: the DFSA register lists Ørsted A/S at 0.54%, last changed 15-10-2026. The baseline's 0.0 is a name-join error, and either way there is no crowded short to squeeze or to signal informed selling.
findings.why_not_priced: Neutral by construction. At 0.54% on a $25m/day name, nobody needs to cover into the print.

findings.finding: The stock rose ~7% intraday on 4 Nov, the session that sets the window's entry close, on the US midterm 'blue wave' and not on company news (Danish wire: 'Ørsted-aktien stiger ved middagstid med 7,5 pct. til 145,93 kr.'). The release opens on an entry price that already carries a macro re-rating, which raises the bar for the US section and adds some give-back risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Ørsted traded down 3% on the 13 Oct Revolution Wind permit remand news and is up ~13% off the 19-20 Oct low (124.85) into the print. There is no measured history of next-day give-back after a macro gap.
findings.original_quote: Ørsted-aktien stiger ved middagstid med 7,5 pct. til 145,93 kr., mens aktien i Vestas stiger med 5 pct. til 207,40 kr. ... Vestas og Ørsted er nogle af dem, der er umiddelbare vindere på det. (Translation: Ørsted shares rise 7.5% at midday to DKK 145.93 while Vestas rises 5% ... Vestas and Ørsted are among the immediate winners.)
findings.why_not_priced: This is an inference about the reaction, not a fact about the print. The run-up IS the price. The point is that the US de-risking is in the entry close, so a release that merely repeats the US timeline adds nothing, while any new US hitch now meets a higher bar.
findings.independence: Investing.com, 'Why is Ørsted stock surging today?', which ties the 7.4% move to the midterms: https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-rsted-stock-surging-today-93CH-4998330

baseline_tension: The lean is mildly negative (−0.45, run-up only), and the stock rose ~8.5% in 5 days, almost all of it on the 4 Nov US midterms rather than company news. The findings are near-neutral to slightly positive on the fundamentals and do not cut against the run-up: the macro re-rating is in the entry price, and the release mostly confirms pre-close drivers.
language_note: The Danish MarketWire/proinvestor wire carried the intraday attribution of the 4 Nov +7.5% move to the US midterms, quoting Danske Bank's head trader; the English Investing.com piece carried the same story, so this is confirmation rather than new information

Otherwise nothing the English sources did not already carry: Ørsted publishes every release in English and Danish at once (the Danish Q1 'Delårsrapport' matched the English), and no Danish-only Q3 preview or consensus surfaced
lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': the pre-close wind/ramp finding cut from +0.3 to +0.1 and the pre-flagged impairment from −0.2 to −0.1
'Macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis': the Vattenfall price proxy for a guidance raise trimmed from +0.4 to +0.3
'The hunter's own caveat has to reach the number': the sell-the-news finding is an inference, trimmed from −0.3 to −0.2, and p_up moved from 53 to 52

'You were right about the number and too small about the move': abs_move_pct raised from 4.0 to 4.5 because the Q3 numbers are new even though the drivers were pre-flagged and the guide is probably reiterated
'`short_ratio_pct: 0.0` ... is not a measurement': prompted the direct register read, which found Ørsted at 0.54% (a name-join miss in the baseline)
